text: For forty years, strange lights have danced over a valley in Norway — and nobody knows what they are.
This is Hessdalen, home to about a hundred and fifty people.
It started in December nineteen eighty-one: a couple saw a burning fireball from their kitchen window.
Within weeks, they appeared up to four times a day — white, yellow, sometimes red — hovering for over an hour, then racing away.
In nineteen eighty-four, scientists came to find out — five weeks, with radar, cameras, and a laser.
They logged a hundred and eighty-eight sightings — radar once tracked one at thirty thousand kilometres an hour.
Then the strangest test: they aimed the laser at a flashing light nine times — and eight times, it changed its rhythm.
Since nineteen ninety-eight, a machine has watched the valley — in two thousand and seven, it caught a light's spectrum: something burning.
Scientists have answers — charged dust, stressed quartz — but none has been proven.
Forty years of data, and the lights of Hessdalen are still unexplained.
So what do you think they are? Tell us in the comments.
